parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The `next` of a previous page, opaque to the client; lines with timestamp >= after, ascending.

parameters.name: task_run
parameters.description: Repeatable, up to 100 UUIDs. Without it: flow-level lines only. With one or more: those task runs' own lines (several make up a process's scope: its marker plus its steps).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The orchestrator's own log text search, sent as a quoted phrase; at most 200 characters.

ErrorEnvelope.description: Normalised client-side by @periplo/core/api; never inspected by screens.

group_by.description: Labels the explorer nests by, outermost first. Empty groups by database alone.

partitions.description: The heaviest partitions in value order, read from the log. May be fewer than partitions_total.

archive_enabled.description: Whether the caller may archive and restore ETLs (kept by Periplo; nothing changes in the orchestrator). The open-core default follows PERIPLO_ETL_ALLOW_ARCHIVE, else PERIPLO_ETL_ALLOW_OPERATE.

archive_mode.description: process: archives are kept in this API process, lost on restart and not shared between API workers (the open-core store); durable: a store that outlives it.

facets.description: How the installation names the facets its tags form, by tag prefix (PERIPLO_ETL_FACETS); empty when it configures none. Nothing in the console names a prefix: every prefix:value tag forms a facet, and tags without a colon one Labels facet.

label.description: Its name; the prefix, humanised, when null.

order.description: Its place among the facets, lowest first; unset ones follow by how many ETLs carry the prefix.

hidden.description: Never offered as a filter, a grouping or on an ETL's page.

role.description: reads/writes: lineage. expects_schedule: an ETL carrying one of values should be scheduled.

values.description: Required by, and only allowed with, role expects_schedule.

by.description: The caller's subject; null without a login.

etl.description: The ETL whose completed run starts this one.

passes.description: The parameters the trigger copies from the upstream run onto the run it starts, by name, sorted.

sets.description: The parameters the trigger sets to a constant on the run it starts, with their value. One set by any other template is in neither.

EtlTrigger.description: What starts a chained ETL: another ETL's run completing.

attempt_started_at.description: When its current (or, once finished, its last) attempt started. start_at is the orchestrator's own start, which a retry from its UI keeps at the first attempt's: elapsed time, slowness and a live bar run from this one. null while the run waits to start, a retried run waiting for its next attempt included. For a finished retried run whose attempts were not read, the first start.

waiting_since.description: Since when it has waited for its current attempt to start: when it was due, or, for a retried run waiting for its next attempt, when it entered its current state or, if later, when that state is due (a retry delay); the orchestrator keeps the first attempt's expected start. The console calls a run stuck from this.

created_by.description: Who created the run, as the orchestrator names them. null for a run an automation created: its name can carry a hidden upstream ETL's name, so the console says "Triggered by X › run" from triggered_by_run instead.

trigger.description: automation when an orchestrator automation created the run (a chained ETL), scheduled when it carries the orchestrator's own auto-scheduled marker, else manual

external_url.description: A deep link into the orchestrator's own UI, or null when none is configured.

attempts.description: One entry per attempt when run_count > 1; null when run_count <= 1 or the response's attempt budget was already spent.

run_count.description: How many attempts the run took (FlowRun.run_count): known even when attempts is not, so a retried run is always marked as such.

expected_start_at.description: When it was due: dates a run that never started (cancelled before it did).

attempts.description: Copied from the FlowRun it derives from; same rules as FlowRun.attempts.

accepts_processes.description: processes appears in parameter_openapi_schema.properties; gates "Re-run from failed process"

external_url.description: A deep link into the orchestrator's own UI, or null when none is configured.

triggered_by.description: The ETL whose completed run starts this one, when an orchestrator automation chains them; only ETLs in the same list are named.

triggers.description: The ETLs this one's completed run starts, sorted; only ETLs in the same list.

archived.description: When the ETL was archived in Periplo, by whom and why; null for an active one. An archived ETL is left out of the list's summary and history; its live runs stay in running.

EtlCurrent.description: Where a running run is right now: its process, step, and position among them. total counts processes seen so far in this run, not the deployment's typical process count (documented limitation).

expected_start_at.description: When it was due to start. For a run that has not started (no start time; PENDING here), it says how long the run has waited: the console calls it stuck once it is more than an hour past it.

typical_seconds.description: Median duration of the deployment's COMPLETED entries in recent.

EtlHistory.description: One window of the dashboard's pulse: bucketed run counts, oldest to newest.

upcoming.description: SCHEDULED runs due in the next 6h, at most 50, soonest first.

running.description: ETLs with a run going: one that has started (RUNNING, or PENDING with a start time) in running, or a newest recent run that has. A run that has not started is waiting, never running.

running_truncated.description: running was capped at 20 entries. The runs waiting to start appended after the cap (at most 5) do not count, so running can hold up to 25 entries.

terminal.description: state in COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED, CRASHED

state_since.description: When the run entered its current state: how long it has been cancelling, before a force.

triggered_by_run.description: For a run an automation created: the upstream ETL's run that started it, read as that ETL's newest run completed before this one was created, preferring one whose passed parameters match this run's.

triggered_runs.description: For a completed run: each downstream ETL's run its automations created after it ended, the first per downstream ETL. A downstream ETL with none did not run.

RunLink.description: A run of another ETL a run is chained to.

noise.description: Starts with one of PERIPLO_ETL_LOG_NOISE's prefixes; folded by default in the web.

task_run_id.description: Opaque id of the step or process that logged the line (as in RunTasks); null for run-level lines.

StepTry.description: One try of a step that failed and was started again in the same attempt: loom makes a task run each time a step starts, so each try is its own task run.

Step.description: One step of a process. A step started again after failing is one step: its state and task_run_id are its last try's, its span from its first try's start to its last try's end, and tries lists each; null for a step that ran once.

runs.description: Oldest to newest, left to right.

processes.description: Order of first appearance in the most recent run that has any, then any others.

truncated.description: A marker, failed-step or mark query hit its hard page cap before exhausting.

next.description: Raw timestamp of the last entry, the received `after` if the page was empty, else null.

truncated.description: True when the page came full (entries.length == limit).

parameters.description: null runs with the deployment's own parameters.

force.description: Force a run stuck cancelling for 10 minutes to cancelled; it stops nothing still running.
